question: Is the domain-model raw score (stream B) available on the trades this study needs to protect, or is its availability determined by the outcome the way the in-domain-flagged stream (A) is?
answer: Available. Coverage is complete on all three primary outcome groups, with a healthy observation count even on the shortest-lived failures. Stream A's 7.7% coverage on failures was an artifact of the established-regime contract gate, not of score availability.

probability_present_rate_by_in_domain_fl.note: Over all 5,665,103 RTH score rows. The model emits a probability at essentially the same rate whether or not it is in-domain; the ~8% of nulls are feature-incompleteness, not gating.

contrast_with_stream_a.stream_a_verdict: UNUSABLE - availability determined by outcome (established gate opens a median 352-448s after confirmation; failed trades die at a median 217-300s)

caveat: Stream B reads each model outside its contractual domain. The number is causally available at runtime, but the frozen percentile thresholds (Top-10/5/2.5/1) were calibrated in-domain and DO NOT apply to it. Threshold-loss events from the brief are therefore NOT APPLICABLE on this stream and must not be synthesised from new cutoffs.
